The retrieved sources present two mutually exclusive positions on whether a degree is necessary to become a successful graphic designer. One cluster (d1, d6, d7) states that most employers require or strongly prefer a bachelor’s degree for graphic design roles, with d6 noting that a bachelor’s degree greatly improves job prospects and d1 specifying a minimum of a bachelor’s degree for most positions. Another cluster (d2, d3, d4, d9, d10) asserts that a degree is not required, emphasizing that employers often hire based on portfolio and experience rather than education, and that many successful designers are self-taught.

Intermediate sources (d5, d8) acknowledge both perspectives, stating that while many positions require degrees, self-taught designers with strong portfolios can succeed. These differing viewpoints within the same scope and time frame reflect genuine conflicting opinions and research outcomes.
